categories.label: Biopesticide
categories.description: A biopesticide comes from natural materials such as bacteria, minerals, or plant extracts. They are generally lower-toxicity to people than conventional pesticides, though not always harmless.

categories.label: California Restricted Material
categories.description: An active ingredient California restricts because of its hazard to people or the environment. Applying one needs a permit from the county agricultural commissioner and a notice of intent before each application, which is why these show up in SprayDays.

categories.label: Carcinogen
categories.description: California lists this chemical as known to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. Being on the list means the state has evidence of a hazard, not that any particular exposure will hurt you.

categories.label: Cholinesterase Inhibitor
categories.description: This chemical works by blocking an enzyme the nervous system needs, in insects and in people. Farmworkers who handle it are required to have regular blood tests.

categories.label: Developmental Toxin
categories.description: California lists this chemical as known to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. Being on the list means the state has evidence of a hazard, not that any particular exposure will hurt you.

categories.label: Fumigant
categories.description: A fumigant is applied to soil or stored crops and becomes a gas that can drift beyond the field. Fumigant applications need extra setbacks and buffer zones, and they are the notices SprayDays publishes 48 hours ahead.

categories.label: Groundwater Contaminant
categories.description: This chemical has been found in California groundwater or can reach it, so the state restricts where and how it is used to protect drinking-water wells.

categories.label: Oil
categories.description: Petroleum or plant oils used to smother insects and mites. They are low in toxicity to people, but they are counted by weight, so they often top the pounds-applied lists.

categories.label: Reproductive Toxin
categories.description: California lists this chemical as known to cause cancer, birth defects, or other reproductive harm. Being on the list means the state has evidence of a hazard, not that any particular exposure will hurt you.

categories.label: Toxic Air Contaminant
categories.description: The California Air Resources Board lists this chemical as an air pollutant that may cause serious illness. Pesticides on the list get extra monitoring and rules when they are sprayed.

narrows.label: Flagged chemicals
narrows.description: Chemicals on a Prop 65 list (carcinogen, reproductive or developmental toxin), CARB's Toxic Air Contaminants, California's restricted materials, or IARC groups 1, 2A and 2B.

narrows.label: Restricted materials
narrows.description: Products California restricts (CDPR's per-product restricted-material flag, or a restricted ingredient when CDPR does not list the product). A property of the product, unlike category=california_restricted.

narrows.label: Fumigants
narrows.description: Products classified as fumigants. A property of the product, unlike category=fumigant.

narrows.label: Applied by air
narrows.description: Applications reported as made by aircraft (CDPR's application method A)
